# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 27 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 27 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_027_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 2 — Simplicity and Giving

**1** He said: "Live with simplicity and innocence. Be like small children who know nothing of the wickedness that eats away at human life. **2** Don't talk badly about anyone. And don't enjoy it when someone else does — because if you listen with pleasure to slander, you share in that person's sin. Even if you haven't said anything yourself, you're guilty for taking pleasure in hearing it. **3** No slander. Nothing but good words about everyone. Affirm what is good in all people; don't add to their sins or take away from their virtues." **4** "When you give, give freely — don't hold back and don't grumble about it. You'll find out who it is that truly rewards generosity. **5** Give to anyone who needs something. Don't stop to judge whether they deserve it or not. Just give — because God wants his gifts to flow through you to everyone. It's on the recipients to answer to God for what they did with what they received. The person who genuinely needed it won't be judged. The one who took it under false pretenses will pay for that. **6** But you as the giver? You're clean. God gave you the instruction to give to all — you just have to fulfill that faithfully. **7** Live this simplicity and you will live to God. Everyone who lives this way will live to God."

---

*PNEUMA note: The radical generosity ethic here echoes the Didache's instruction on giving (Did. 1.5-6) — very similar language about giving without questioning the recipient's worthiness.*
